newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close slightly lower on rate worries.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close slightly lower on rate worries.

text.p: French stocks faded at session end on Wednesday to close slightly lower as questions about the direction of interest rates in Europe weighed on markets.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 0.98 points or 0.05 percent at 2124.76 after spending nearly the entire day in positive territory. CAC-40 futures were down 12 points.

The index failed to benefit from a small rise in U.S. stocks after U.S. third-quarter gross domestic product growth rose 2.2 percent after second-quarter growth of 4.7 percent. U.S. debt markets lost ground near the end of the day, which added another negative factor for French shares.
Volume was 4.8 billion francs of which 3.2 billion francs on CAC-40 shares.

The surprise quarter-point official interest rate increase in Britain pushed the FTSE 100 index lower and combined with comments earlier in the week on German interest rates produced some caution on the part of investors, traders said.

Predictions from U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs that the U.S. Federal Reserve would raise U.S. interest rates by 1.25 percent in the next 12 to 18 months also prompted some questions about the direction of rates in Europe.
"You can't really say there are worries, but investors prefer to remain cautious because of interest rates but also because of upcoming U.S. data," said one trader.
It was the third consecutive drop for Paris shares and brought them back to their levels at the beginning of October.
Many dealers said they expected the bourse to drop again on Thursday. The bourse is closed Friday for All Saints Day.
French car maker PSA Peugeot-Citroen was the biggest loser on the day, down 4.29 percent on worries about its outlook now that a government car-buying incentive programme has ended.

Luxury flagship LVMH rose 3.41 percent on news it would spend 12.6 billion francs to take control of U.S. based duty free chain DFS. LVMH shrugged off an announcement that S&P put LVMH short-term paper on watch with negative implications.
Books-to-missiles conglomerate Lagardere closed up 2.98 percent as dealers continued to believe it will win the bidding for Thomson SA despite public outcry over the decision.
Equipment manufacturer Sidel closed 3.98 percent higher making it the day's biggest gainer on higher nine-month sales and brighter profit outlook.
